referenceCard.title: Names and values

subtitle: A name is a label on a value. = moves the label; print shows what's there.

teach.body:
x = 5 means: work out the right side, then stick the name x on that value. Python runs lines top to bottom, one at a time. When it reaches a line that uses a name, it uses whatever that name holds at that moment.

So after
  a = 5
  b = a
  a = 6
b is still 5. b was given a's value when line 2 ran. It doesn't follow a around afterwards.
teach.title: = is an instruction, not an equation

teach.body: 3 is a number. "3" is a string: text that happens to contain the character 3. + adds numbers but joins strings, so 3 + 4 is 7 while "3" + "4" is "34". Mixing them, as in 3 + "4", stops the program with a TypeError. Convert first with int("4") or str(3).
teach.title: Numbers and strings

teach.body: print(a, b) shows a, then one space, then b, and ends the line. Strings appear without their quotes. Inside the trace panel you'll see repr values, where strings keep their quotes ('Ada'), so you can tell "7" from 7.
